Action.description:
An action to execute as part of a command

`EnumDiscriminants` generates the fieldless [`ActionDiscriminants`] with
`EnumIter` — the consistency canary iterates it to assert every variant is
either wired into the UI type registry or explicitly exempt.

oneOf.description: Open an application or a file through the host OS.
Select one random number or weighted text value.
Control music playback (play, pause, next, previous, etc.)
Send prompt to AI, store result (non-streaming, no chat output)
Stream AI response to chat with optional TTS
Take a screenshot (save to file or store in variable)
Click a UI element using Windows UI Automation
Type text into a UI element using Windows UI Automation
Search YouTube and open a video in the browser
Run another saved command inline (compose/reuse commands).
Ask the companion to play an animation — enter a state, or raise a token.
Enable or disable the desktop companion's visual body.

Start a «Рабочий» task in the background — a ROUTINE: a saved, repeatable
job (`work-mode` builds; elsewhere the executor refuses it).

Replay a recorded input macro (keyboard + mouse).

The most dangerous action in the product: a step list can drive any
program the user can. See [`MacroAction`](crate::command::MacroAction).

A dynamically-registered action type (for plugins).
The `handler_id` references a registered ActionHandler.

AiRequestAction.description: AI request — send prompt, store result, no chat output

include_context.description: Include conversation context from chat history

store_result_in.description: Variable name to store the AI response in

CatalogueProvenance.description:
Where a command installed from the Workshop's CATALOGUE came from: the catalogue item, the
version installed, and the SHA-256 of the artefact that version served (catalogue core §39,
C7). It is the catalogue's twin of [`MarketplaceSource`] and is set only by the catalogue's
commands installer, never by a save request; the portable form clears it
(`command::portable::portable_command`), as it does `marketplace_source`.

artefact_sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the artefact that version served.

store_in.description: Variable to store result for get operation

CommandExecutionOverride.description:
Per-command override of the global execution budget
([`crate::config::CommandExecutionSettings`]).

Each field is independent: `None` = inherit the global default; `Some(n)`
overrides it, with the SAME sentinel meaning as the global setting — a `0`
ceiling falls back to the engine default, and `timeout_seconds == 0` means
**no** wall-clock deadline. This lets one command opt into "no time limit"
even when the global has one (a long-running monitor), while a quick command
caps itself with a small timeout — the whole point of a per-command budget.

max_loop_iterations.description: Override for a single loop node's iteration ceiling. `None` = inherit.

max_steps.description: Override for the run's step ceiling. `None` = inherit global.

timeout_seconds.description:
Override for the wall-clock deadline in seconds. `None` = inherit;
`Some(0)` = explicitly no time limit.

CompanionAnimationAction.description:
Ask the companion to play something.

# Two fields of VALUE under one `mode` key, and never one shared field

A node is a DOCUMENT that gets edited. A user who flips the dropdown to look
at the other mode and flips back must find their own value where they left
it — and with one shared field the flip REINTERPRETS it: a state name
delivered as a trigger token matches no out-edge under any state, so it is a
permanent, silent no-op. That is the exact outcome
`astra_daemon::companion::animation` exists to refuse, and it would arrive
here by an edit nobody considered an edit. The second `String` makes it
impossible rather than unlikely.

Both values support `{variable}` substitution, resolved against the run's
context before the cue is built — so a trigger slot can carry the state name.

mode.description:
`state` — enter a state and let the ENGINE pick the variant by that
state's own weighted / shuffle / sequential policy — or `trigger`, raise
a token into the state graph and take the current state's matching
out-edge.

A CLOSED set, and anything else is an error at execution time rather
than a default: `Cue::from_mode` answers `None`, and defaulting would
send one mode's value down the other mode's arm. Empty preserves a
document written before a mode existed — which is also an error, and
deliberately so.

state.description: The state to enter, read only when `mode == "state"`.

trigger.description: The token to raise, read only when `mode == "trigger"`.

CompanionSwitch.description:
What a companion node does to the setting. `Toggle` reads the setting when
the node runs, not when it was saved.

action.description: Action to perform: play, pause, toggle, next, previous, stop

handler_id.description: Handler identifier — maps to a registered ActionHandler

params.description: Arbitrary parameters as a JSON object

config.description: Arbitrary configuration as a JSON object

handler_id.description: Handler identifier — maps to a plugin trigger type (e.g. `plugin__dice_roller__on_natural_20`)

oneOf.description: Legacy sequential action list — not used at runtime.
Visual node-graph editor (all commands use this).

ExecuteAction.description:
Execute a program or command.

The `shell` field selects the runner:
- empty → the OS default shell (PowerShell on Windows, `$SHELL`/`sh` on Unix),
- a shell id (`"powershell"`, `"cmd"`, `"bash"`, `"zsh"`, `"fish"`, …) → run
  `command` as a script in that shell, capturing its output,
- [`EXECUTE_OPEN_MODE`] (`"open"`) → open `path` with `arguments` via the OS
  shell association (like the Windows Run dialog / `xdg-open`).

arguments.description: Arguments passed to the opened target (open-mode only).

capture_output.description:
Capture stdout/stderr/exit code and surface them (shell modes).
Defaults to true — the user wants to see real output and errors.

command.description: Command/script to execute (shell modes), possibly multiline.

icon_path.description:
A picture the user chose by hand for the companion's app badge, and it
OVERRIDES whatever the daemon would extract from `path` (open-mode only).

It exists because extraction has no chance at all on some targets: a
`.url` launcher and a wrapper script *are* the file that gets opened, and
neither carries the icon of the application it starts. Without a manual
answer those launches draw no badge, which on screen is indistinguishable
from the companion being switched off — so the user is given the one
thing the extractor cannot infer.

`#[serde(default)]` is what keeps every `commands.json` written before
this field readable: the absent key reads as empty, empty means "no
override", and extraction behaves exactly as it did.

shell.description: Runner: empty = OS default shell, a shell id, or `"open"` (open-mode).

show_window.description:
Open an interactive terminal window instead of capturing (shell modes).
Mutually exclusive with capture.

GraphNode.description: A single node in the workflow graph.

data.description:
Configuration data for this node (action fields, etc.).

Deliberately FREE-FORM — a bag the UI, the AI tools and every node
kind write their own keys into (`action_type`/`action`/`config`,
`trigger_type`, `disabled`, `wait_for_completion`, …), none of it
enforced at this layer; only the graph executor and `GraphNode`'s own
readers give any of those keys meaning. `deserialize_node_data`
(`opening.rs`) migrates a couple of legacy spellings in place before
the map is built, but never refuses a shape, so the schema says exactly
what the type is — any object — and invents no structure the
deserializer does not itself enforce.

id.description: Unique node ID (typically a UUID string).

position_x.description: X position on the editor canvas.

position_y.description: Y position on the editor canvas.

KeyDir.description: Whether a key step presses, releases, or does both.

oneOf.description: Press and release — the common case.
Press and leave held (a later `Up` step releases it).

MacroAction.description:
Replay a recorded input macro.

Every field defaults, so a freshly dropped node (`config: {}`) deserializes —
which is what lets the generic workflow-graph pre-deserializer handle this
action with no arm of its own.

note.description:
Provenance written by the recorder ("Recorded 2026-07-28 · 41 steps ·
12.4 s"). Free text; the user may edit or clear it.

repeat.description:
How many times to run the whole list. `0` is coerced to `1` — an
accidental infinity here would be a macro nobody can stop.

speed.description:
Playback speed multiplier. **Divides** every delay: 2.0 replays twice as
fast. Clamped to 0.25..=10.0 at execute time.

MacroCoordinateMode.description: How a macro's coordinates are interpreted at playback.

oneOf.description: Virtual-desktop screen pixels. Breaks if the target window moves.

Relative to the window that was focused while recording, re-found by
class and title at playback. Survives the window moving; fails loudly
(never clicks the bare desktop) when the window is gone.

MacroDelayMode.description: Where a macro's timing comes from at playback.

oneOf.description: Ignore recorded timing; wait `fixed_delay_ms` before every step.

Replay as fast as the OS accepts. Fine for text, usually too fast for
UI that animates.

MacroStep.description:
One step of a recorded macro.

Internally tagged on `op`, so the wire shape, the JSON stored in a workflow
node's `config`, and this enum are all the same vocabulary — the frontend
never translates.

oneOf.description: A run of typed characters, coalesced from individual keystrokes.
A modifier chord (Ctrl+C). Pressed in order, released in reverse.
Move the pointer without clicking. Only recorded during a drag.
Move then press-and-release. `clicks: 2` is a double-click.
Move then press and hold (a later `MouseUp` releases it).

An explicit pause. The recorder never emits one — timing lives on
`delay_before_ms`; this is for the user to insert in the editor.
A labelled divider. Does nothing; makes a long list readable.

MarketplaceSource.description: Tracks where a command was installed from in the marketplace

MouseButton.description:
Mouse button.

`X1`/`X2` are the side buttons (Back/Forward on most mice). They exist
because a *recorded* macro can contain one — the alternative was a second
button enum living next to this one. The `mouse_click` action's dropdown
deliberately still offers only the three primary buttons; a type wider than
the UI offers is safe, the reverse is not.

button.description:
Button to click. `deserialize_mouse_button` accepts this field's own
lowercase name OR any case of it, OR the legacy numeric encoding
(0-4) a recorded macro can carry — wider than [`MouseButton`]'s own
derived schema, so the field's schema is built from that acceptance
directly rather than from the Rust type.

NodeType.description: The kind of a graph node.

oneOf.description: Entry point of the graph. Exactly one per workflow.
Executes an `Action` (same types as the linear editor).
Trigger entry point — replaces Start with trigger configuration.
Multi-way branching based on expression matching.

OpenApplicationAction.description:
Cross-platform Open node. The persisted tag stays `open_application` so
existing commands keep their identity.

app_id.description:
Application target: a `.desktop` id on Linux, or an Apps-folder target /
executable path on Windows.

app_name.description:
Human-readable name, stored by the picker for display when the app
isn't installed on the running machine.

args.description: Optional extra arguments appended to the launch command.

icon_path.description:
A picture the user chose by hand for the companion's app badge, and it
OVERRIDES whatever the daemon would extract from the `.desktop` entry.

It exists because extraction has no chance at all on some targets: most
entries name an icon by THEME name, and a theme this daemon cannot read
resolves to nothing at all (`LINUX_PARITY_DEBT.md`) — as does an entry
that simply declares no icon. A launch that draws no badge looks exactly
like the companion being switched off, so the user is given the one
thing the extractor cannot infer.

`#[serde(default)]` is what keeps every `commands.json` written before
this field readable: the absent key reads as empty, empty means "no
override", and extraction behaves exactly as it did.

OpenMode.description: What the cross-platform Open node opens. Missing on legacy Linux app nodes.

mode.description: "url" = open given URL; "search" = build search URL from search_query

search_query.description: Search query text (used when mode == "search"); opens e.g. Google search

path.description: Sound file path or built-in name

combinations.description: Additional chords, each with a delay after the preceding chord releases.

RunCommandAction.description:
Run another saved command inline.

References the target by its `command` NAME (matched case-insensitively,
like the AI `execute_command` tool) so the picker and the graph node show
the human-readable name directly. `input` optionally seeds the sub-command's
`original_input` / `{capture}` so a sub-command that reads `{input}` /
`{capture}` receives a value; it supports `{variable}` substitution against
the parent context. Recursion / cycles are bounded centrally in
`graph_executor::execute_graph` via the execution `command_stack`.

command.description: Name of the saved command to run (case-insensitive match).

input.description:
Optional input passed to the sub-command (seeds its `original_input` /
`{capture}`). Supports `{variable}` substitution. Default empty.

mode.description:
Operation mode: `save` writes a PNG, `ask_ai` sends the capture to AI.
Empty preserves commands saved before modes were introduced.

monitor_index.description: Monitor index (0 = primary, used when window_name is empty)

save_path.description:
Save directory (supports variables). In `save` mode, empty uses system Pictures.
Legacy commands without a mode use a literal file path, or base64 when empty.

store_in.description: Variable name to store result (file path or base64)

window_name.description:
Window name to capture (empty = full screen)

Kept for backwards compatibility with hand-written/AI-created commands.
The Commands editor does not expose window or region selection.

ScrollAxis.description:
Wheel axis. Positive `clicks` is up (vertical) / right (horizontal) — the OS
convention; `InputSession::scroll` owns the conversion to enigo's.

SetCompanionEnabledAction.description:
Persist the companion on/off setting, shared with the AI tool of the same name.

Saved before `state` existed as `{"enabled": bool}`; that spelling is still
read (`state` wins when both are present) and never written.

`#[serde(from = "SetCompanionEnabledWire")]` means the struct's own field
(`state: CompanionSwitch`, required) is NOT the wire shape — the wire accepts
`SetCompanionEnabledWire`'s two optional fields instead, defaulting when
neither is present. `#[schemars(with = "SetCompanionEnabledWire")]` makes the
SCHEMA built from that wire struct too, so it does not claim `state` is
required when the real deserializer never does.

value.description:
Volume value as string (supports variables like {myVar}).
Parsed to f64 at runtime. Range: 0-100 for "set", any signed value for "add".

tts_pitch.description: TTS pitch (0.5–2.0) when use_settings_voice is false

tts_speed.description: TTS speed (0.5–2.0) when use_settings_voice is false

use_settings_voice.description:
When true, use the voice from app settings; when false, use this
node's own `voices` / `tts_speed` / `tts_pitch`.

voices.description:
Per-provider voice memory for this node (used when `use_settings_voice`
is false). The TTS provider is always the globally-selected one — this
node no longer overrides it; the voice is resolved against that
provider, falling back to the settings voice when no entry exists.

[`VoiceSelection`] is `#[serde(transparent)]` over a provider→voice
string map, so the schema is built directly from that wire shape
(`voice_selection_schema`) rather than from `crate::voice`, which this
schema does not otherwise reach into.

StreamToChatAction.description: Stream to chat — AI request that streams response to chat and optionally speaks

include_context.description: Include conversation context from chat history

store_result_in.description: Variable name to store the full AI response in

exact_match.description: Disable fuzzy typo matching; every trigger requires the complete phrase.

Trigger.description: A trigger that activates a command

UiClickAction.description: Click a UI element using Windows UI Automation

window_name.description: Window to scope search to (supports variables)

UiTypeAction.description: Type text into a UI element using Windows UI Automation

window_name.description: Window to scope search to (supports variables)

WorkTaskAction.description:
A routine: start a «Рабочий» task in the background, the way «Быстрый» hands
one over (`start_work`), and get its report in the conversation the command
ran in (Goose's recipes — phase 4 of `docs/arcs/ASSISTANT_MODES_PLAN.md`).

`task` is the whole job — the goal, the form of the result, every file and
fact it needs — and supports `{variable}` substitution, so a trigger phrase's
`{slots}` are the routine's parameters. Starting it is all the node does: the
work runs in its own «Рабочий» thread, under the user's permission mode, and
the command moves on at once.

title.description: The card's and the thread's title; empty = taken from the task.

edge_order.description: Authored wire-array order for presentation; run order remains `fan_out`.

edges.description: All edges keyed by their ID.

nodes.description: All nodes keyed by their ID.

YoutubePlayAction.description: Search YouTube and open a video

mode.description: "play" = open first result; "search_results" = return JSON list (no browser open)

description: A CommandDefinition as a .astra file or a Workshop catalogue command artefact carries it — the local fields (id, created_at, updated_at, group_id, enabled, marketplace_source, catalogue_source) are optional here; an installer stamps its own.

actions.description:
Actions to execute.

`deserialize_actions` (`opening.rs`) migrates the legacy
`{"type":"execute","shell":"open",…}` shape to `open_application`
BEFORE each element is decoded as an [`Action`] — but every field that
shape sets (`shell`, `path`, `arguments`) already exists, unconstrained,
on [`ExecuteAction`], so the migration is invisible to this field's
schema: that legacy shape, and today's `open_application` shape, both
already validate as themselves. The schema therefore needs no override
here, only this note.

catalogue_source.description: Workshop catalogue source info (set when the command was installed from the catalogue).

editor_mode.description: Editor mode: linear (action list) or graph (node editor).

execution.description:
Per-command override of the global execution budget. Default (all-`None`)
= inherit the global limits. Resolved at the run root by the daemon's
`resolve_budget`; when this command is called from another (a nested
`run_command`) its override may TIGHTEN the inherited budget but never
loosen it past the root's wall-clock cap.

group_id.description: Group (folder) this command belongs to. `None` = ungrouped.

marketplace_source.description: Marketplace source info (set when command was installed from marketplace)

priority.description:
Text-matching priority. Higher levels are considered before lower ones;
commands on lower levels are ignored once a higher level has a match.
Any integer is accepted and clamped into 1..=10
(`MIN_COMMAND_PRIORITY..=MAX_COMMAND_PRIORITY`); absent defaults to 4
(`DEFAULT_COMMAND_PRIORITY`).

slash_description.description:
One-line label shown next to `/name` in the chat slash menu (e.g. "Turn
into a bullet list"). Deliberately separate from [`Self::description`]:
that one feeds semantic matching (the embeddings index + the voice
prefilter), so a menu subtitle written here can't silently change which
spoken phrases fire the command. Empty = the slash registry falls back to
`description`.

slash_enabled.description:
Whether this command is reachable from chat as a `/name` slash command.
Opt-in (default `false`): only user commands the user explicitly enables
appear in the `/` menu and respond to `/name`. Gated together with
`enabled` + a valid single-token name by the slash registry.
